text:
jordan: Quick q — we're seeing a few requests that include X-Client-Meta: tenant=acme but the bearer token maps to tenant=acme-pro. Currently the gateway favours the header and routes to acme. Should the auth principal always win?

maya: Yes — auth-derived tenant should be canonical for routing + billing. Client-supplied headers are user-controlled and can be spoofed. Headers only ok as an explicit opt-in via signature.

sam: Agreed. FWIW we prototyped a signed header approach last quarter (X-Route-Sig signed with a per-tenant key). If sig verifies and timestamp is within 60s, accept X-Client-Meta for affinity/routing. Otherwise ignore.

jordan: Makes sense. How does that play with UA-based heuristics? We do UA -> mobile shard for known mobile SDKs as a fallback. Example config I have:
```yaml
route_rules:
  - match: path: /v1/generate
    routing_priority: [auth_tenant, signed_header, ua_infer]
    quota_attribution: auth_principal
    fallback: mobile_shard_if_ua_matches
```

kai: Important callout: metrics & quotas must be attributed to the auth principal ALWAYS. Even if the signed header routed to a different tenant for affinity, billing/quotas should follow token. Otherwise accounting gets messy.

leah: Security note — middleboxes or proxies can inject X-Client-Meta. If we accept signed headers, we must stamp requests at the edge with X-Edge-Claim to indicate which verifier accepted it and the verifier id. That way downstream services can decide whether to trust.

infra-bot: "deploy: edge-prop-validation v2 -> canary (10%) scheduled 2026-04-01T03:00:00Z"

sre-oncall: When we flip default to auth-first, watch for a spike in 403/4xx from customers who relied on header routing. I'll add an alert to detect +20% 4xx from any tenant in 5m.

maya: Proposed explicit policy order + surface plan: 
1) auth principal mapping (highest confidence)
2) signed X-Client-Meta verified by edge (verifier must be in allowlist)
3) UA-inferred routing (very low confidence; only used for latency opt-in / mobile shard)
4) no header -> default route

Metrics: add routing_source tag to request logs: one of [auth, signed_header, ua, fallback]. Expose in Console per-request drilldown and in per-route dashboards. Quotas/billing always use auth.

jordan: Can someone make a small PR with the routing order change + metric tag? I'll coordinate the console bits. I'll put a note in the migration doc about the signed header opt-in.

sam: I'll do the PR. TODOs: add unit tests for expired sigs, test spoofed header (unsigned), and update router integration tests for routing_source tag. Also update docs for signing key rotation semantics.

leah: LGTM. :thumbsup:

jordan: Thanks all. I'll drop a short note to accounts slack so PMs know behaviour changed.

sam: One more UX ask — Console request view should show the raw headers (redact tokens) + a small row "routing_source: auth" and an explanation tooltip. Saves us a support ping. :eyes:
